title: StarCar freight ticket (ticket-kind record payload)
description: #84: the ticket contract LAYERED over starcar-artifact/1 (Law 6 - this file does not restate the base record contract; validators run BOTH schemas against a record, same convention as schema/starcar-manifest.schema.json). A ticket is a kind=ticket record representing ONE GitHub Project 6 item currently in Backlog or Todo status (the inbound queue, owner ruling 2026-07-27) - never a dispatch-lifecycle event, never folded (board/fold has no case for kind=ticket; board/assemble reads these raw, exactly as it already reads manifest payloads off intent-kind records via manifestPayload).

ticket.description: The single new top-level key (design DR3-1 item 4's precedent, ported here per #84's owner ruling: ONE key added to the wire schema and every typed decoder's known key-set, so D17's unknown-field disclosure never fires on a well-formed ticket record).

number.description: The GitHub issue number - the one identity fact this record exists to carry. The adapter derives subject (ticket-<number>) FROM this at write time; no downstream reader re-parses the subject string back into a number (Law 6 - one direction of derivation only).

status.description: The project's Status field value at write time (e.g. "Backlog", "Todo") - open vocabulary (Law 7), never schema-enumerated. In practice always one of Backlog/Todo, because the adapter only ever writes items whose status is one of those two (owner ruling: work accepted but not started); a value outside that pair would mean the adapter's own queue filter regressed, not a schema violation.

url.description: The issue's github.com URL, verbatim from `gh project item-list`'s content.url - never reconstructed client-side.

allOf.$comment: RE2-safe form (schema/starcar-manifest.schema.json's SB-1 precedent, folded here rather than rediscovered): a lookahead-free if/then pair expresses 'a record whose kind is NOT ticket must not carry a ticket key', because Go's RE2 regexp engine rejects negative lookaheads that .NET's Test-Json accepts - a schema only one language could load would break the one-schema-both-languages thesis (Law 6, D15).
